lines: Telo Ride starts here: one Angular workspace, and the ride app it builds.
The frontend holds three libraries, api, domain and components, and one application, ride.
Ride uses all three. Domain uses api. Api uses nothing.
Import against that direction and lint fails. And only domain's bluetooth folder may touch navigator dot bluetooth.
Start the app and Home opens in the app shell. The Telo Ride lockup links home, and the main navigation marks Home as the current page.
Every colour is a token from the design system. Barlow Condensed, Inter Tight and JetBrains Mono ship with the app, never from a CDN.
An address that matches no screen says so, with no current item in the header.
On a keyboard, the first Tab reaches Skip to content, and Enter moves focus straight to the page.
The same shell fits a phone, a tablet, a laptop and a desktop. On a phone, the navigation takes its own row.
Every screen is its own chunk, loaded on demand, and the build fails if the first download outgrows its budget.
What the tests prove: six behaviour specs run against the production build, and any page error, or any request off this machine, fails them.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
